title: Positional Encoding as Overlapping Circles
category_reason: Explains transformer sinusoidal positional encoding, a core transformer mechanism.
thesis: Each token position is a point on each of several frequency circles; where all the points converge is a unique 'fingerprint' of that position, visualizing sinusoidal positional encoding as an interference pattern.
key_claims: Each circle represents a frequency dimension; the token's position is a point on each circle via sin/cos of position*frequency.
Small circles = high frequency (fine detail), large circles = low frequency (coarse structure); frequencies follow 1/10000^(2i/d).
The combination of angles across all circles is unique per position, like clock hands — the convergence zone is the unique encoding.
Nearby positions have similar convergence zones, distant positions produce completely different patterns.
The dot product between two positional encodings captures their relative distance (implied by the interference framing).
visualizations: Canvas 2D interactive: overlapping frequency circles with a position point, three modes (interference / connections / field), sliders for position / num-frequencies / sequence-length / compare-position, and spacebar auto-play.
internal_tensions: The 'convergence = unique fingerprint' framing is heuristic rather than a rigorous statement about the embedding.
The 'field' mode renders a full pixel-level interference field and is noted as expensive to recompute.

title: Wenn aus Gedanken Woerter werden (ganz einfach erklaert)
category_reason: Plain-language explainer of an LLM paper on latent semantic manifolds and the expressibility gap.
thesis: Language models 'think' in continuous latent number spaces but always output discrete words from a finite vocabulary; some thoughts never fit exactly into a word, leaving an unavoidable 'unsure zone' the paper calls the Expressibility Gap.
key_claims: The model organizes its data on thin 'sheets' (manifolds) — idea from Ansuini et al. 2019, confirmed for large transformers by Valeriani et al. 2023.
About 40-51% of word predictions fall in the 'unsure zone' (nearly equidistant between two words) across six real models from 124M to 1.5B parameters.
Larger models are on average slightly more confident, but the hardest ~5% of predictions stay equally hard for all models — because the language itself is ambiguous there, not the training.
To halve the error you need roughly 1000x more words, since the thought-space has ~20 effective degrees of freedom (error ~ (1/N)^(2/20)).
Language is a lossy compression of meaning (a map that always leaves something out); the named loss is the 'Expressibility Gap'.
Suggested uses: models could self-report 'I hesitate here', insert new subwords where the unsure zone is widest, and reframe some 'hallucinations' as thoughts sitting on a word boundary.
visualizations: Canvas 2D 'meadow of words': nearest-word Voronoi region with a gold boundary (unsure) zone; hover to read winner word, win-probability, and gap fraction; sliders for vocabulary size and temperature; all local in-browser.
internal_tensions: Admitted simplifications: the field is 2D vs ~20D real, words are randomly placed vs semantically placed, and the 'unsure zone' is measured by geometric distance vs the paper's margin.
The 'floor' that no technique can reach rests on the intrinsic-dimension / covering-rate argument applied to real language.

title: Boundary maps by hand — the pictures
category_reason: Pure algebraic-topology pedagogy (simplices, boundary operator) with no AI application.
thesis: A shape is glued from simplices and the boundary map records each piece's edge/rim/skin; walking through orientation, head/tail, chains, and the animated boundary of a triangle explains why boundary-of-boundary is zero and how Betti numbers count holes.
key_claims: An n-simplex has n+1 corners and lives in n dimensions: point, edge, triangle, tetrahedron.
Ordering vertices by index puts arrows on edges (low to high index), fixing an orientation; swapping two vertices flips the sign.
The boundary of an edge is head minus tail: partial[v_i, v_j] = v_j - v_i.
The boundary of a triangle is built by a ritual — delete each vertex in turn, giving +[v1,v2] - [v0,v2] + [v0,v1] with signs (-1)^i.
partial o partial = 0: at each corner a +1 (one edge's head) meets a -1 (the next edge's tail) and cancels, so a rim has no ends.
Holes are counted by Betti numbers b_n = (# n-simplices) - rank partial_n - rank partial_{n+1}: clusters, loops, hollow voids.
visualizations: Static canvas drawings (four simplices, oriented edge/triangle, head/tail, chain 2a+b-c, partial*partial=0 cancellation) plus one animated canvas stepping through deleting each vertex of a triangle with a pause/play button and a paper-pencil exercise with a reveal-answer spoiler.
internal_tensions: It is deliberately a minimal, intuition/formalism/example teaching doc with no application, so its only open question is why one would learn this (no AI link provided here).

title: Geometrische Visuelle Halluzinationen — Interaktiv
category_reason: Physics/dynamical-systems account of hallucination patterns in the biological visual cortex, not ML.
thesis: Geometric visual hallucinations (Kluver's form constants) arise from Turing-type pattern formation in V1, and the log-polar retino-cortical map turns simple cortical activity stripes into spirals, tunnels, and grids in the visual field.
key_claims: Kluver (1920s) classified hallucination patterns under mescaline into 4 form constants: tunnels/funnels, spirals, grids/honeycombs, spiderwebs.
Ermentrout & Cowan (1979) gave the first mathematical model: V1 activity forms periodic patterns via Turing instability (bifurcation + group theory).
Bressloff et al. (2001) added orientation selectivity and Euclidean symmetry (shift-twist), explaining all Kluever form constants.
The retino-cortical map is x = ln(r), y = theta: circles map to vertical lines, rays to horizontal lines, spirals to diagonal lines; so V1 stripes appear as spirals/tunnels/grids.
The dispersion relation lambda(q) = -1 + mu * w_hat(q) decides which wavelength destabilizes first; short-range excitation = activator, long-range inhibition = inhibitor.
Goldenfeld (2018): we do not constantly hallucinate because sparse inhibitory connections suppress spontaneous patterns, which drugs then disturb.
methods_math: Euclidean group E(2) and axial subgroups (planforms)
visualizations: Canvas pattern generators comparing V1 (cortex) vs the visual field via inverse log-polar mapping, with a pattern selector and wave-number slider; a Plotly dispersion-relation plot with excitability and inhibition-range sliders; a live 2D Wilson-Cowan simulation (start/reset/speed); and planform tabs (rolls/squares/hexagons).
internal_tensions: It is a physics/model of a biological system, not of an artificial network — the 'neural computation' citations do not make it ML.
The stochastic-Turing suppression account (why we don't always hallucinate) is a proposed mechanism, not fully established.

title: AttentionViz — Interaktive Erklärun (Yeh et al. 2023)
category_reason: Explains a transformer-attention interpretability tool (joint Q/K embedding, global head view).
thesis: AttentionViz projects Queries and Keys into a shared 2D space so that nearby points mean high attention, giving a global (matrix) view of what each head generally does across thousands of examples, instead of one sentence at a time.
key_claims: Attention depends on the Q-K dot product, which is closely related to distance, so nearby points in the plot correspond to high attention — the head's shape becomes a visual signature.
Trick 1 (Key-Translation): softmax is translation-invariant, so all keys can be shifted by a constant vector without changing attention, letting the two clouds be centered together.
Trick 2 (QK-Skalierung): scaling queries by c and keys by 1/c preserves the dot product but changes visual distance; c is chosen so distance correlates optimally with attention.
Empirically in BERT the average Spearman correlation between Query-Key distance and dot product is about -0.938 (near-perfect negative).

Findings: BERT heads show 'positional spirals' and semantic clusters; ViT heads sort patches by brightness, hue, and frequency/angle; GPT-2 shows an 'attend-to-first' anomaly with large Query/Key norm differences (~ -4.6 average).
Builds on Activation Atlas (Carter et al.), t-SNE/UMAP/PCA, and BertViz (Vig 2019).
visualizations: Canvas attention demo (drag a query; circle size = attention to each key), a trick canvas with translation/scale sliders to mix the Q/K clouds, a Plotly distance-vs-dot-product scatter, a canvas morph between a positional spiral and semantic clusters, and a Plotly ViT hue/frequency scatter; Temml for the equations.
internal_tensions: Distance is a proxy for attention (a correlation, not an identity); the 'nahe Punkte = hohe Attention' claim is approximate.
Several plots (e.g. the -0.94 correlation) use simulated/illustrative data in this page even though the paper reports real BERT numbers.

title: Lens Focus Explorer — Image on Ground
category_reason: An image-interpolation/super-resolution demo about a focus limit, with no ML model.
thesis: A lens-focus tool over an image lying on a ground plane: focusing a region past its native resolution produces 'hallucination' — detail that is interpolated, not real data — making the information limit of reconstruction tangible.
key_claims: Focus level maps to a blur: low focus = large block-averaging; at native resolution it switches to bilinear interpolation.
Focus beyond native resolution (level above a NATIVE_THRESHOLD of 7) means sampling/interpolating beyond the real data, labeled 'HALLUCINATION'.
Focus is blended smoothly across the 3x3 neighboring cells with Gaussian weights so transitions are seamless.
Hallucinating cells are tinted red/magenta and badged; live stats show average focus and the count of hallucinating cells.
Any same-folder image can be loaded; otherwise a generated smiley pattern is used as fallback.
visualizations: CSS 3D ground plane with a 6x5 grid of lenses: left-click to focus, right-click to defocus, scroll wheel for fine control; per-pixel rendering with focus-dependent sampling and red 'hallucination' tinting; live stats row.
internal_tensions: 'Hallucination' here means interpolation beyond available data, not generative-model hallucination — the metaphor borrows ML language for a purely classical image-processing limit.

title: Process & Reality — Interaktiv Erleben (A.N. Whitehead)
category_reason: Interactive guide to Whitehead's process philosophy; no ML content.
thesis: Whitehead's process philosophy holds that reality is made of 'actual entities' — drops of experience — not things; process/becoming replaces substance, and creativity is the ultimate principle by which the many become one and are increased by one.
key_claims: The fundamental building blocks of reality are 'actual entities' (drops of experience), not dead matter particles — an anti-materialist stance.
Process over substance: nothing simply 'is', everything 'becomes' (concrescence); each moment is a new actual occasion.
Principle of relativity: every entity is a potential for every becoming; the universe is a network of mutual 'prehensions'.
Each actual entity has a 'subjective aim' — an inner teleology, so final causality runs alongside efficient causality.
'Eternal objects' (colors, forms, math structures) are pure potentials that 'ingress' into concrete experiences.
'Creativity' is the ultimate principle: the many become one and are increased by one.
Dipolar theology: God has a primordial nature (order of all possibilities) and a consequent nature; God is 'Poet of the World' who lures rather than coerces, so freedom is real.
Objective immortality / 'perpetual perishing': past entities live on as objective data for all future experiences.
visualizations: Particle-network background canvas, a 'Concrescence' simulation (scattered data points merge into one unit = 'satisfaction'), clickable discovery cards with a progress/score bar, a philosophy genealogy timeline, and two multiple-choice quizzes.
internal_tensions: Panexperientialism (even electrons 'prehend') is in direct tension with scientific materialism, which the page flags as 'anti-materialism'.
A non-coercive, luring God is a contested middle position between classical theism and naturalism.

title: Attention = Points That Pull Each Other Closer
category_reason: Models transformer attention as point motion and reads its output as a simplicial complex of meaning.
thesis: Attention makes each word (a point in meaning-space) move toward the points it finds relevant; the simplicial complex (edges and triangles) that forms shows where words clump together — that clumping is the 'meaning' attention composes.
key_claims: Each word is a point in a 3D semantic space with axes [gender, being, power].
Relevance score(i,j) is the dot product (the Q-K part), treated as a similarity measure.
Each word then moves to the weighted center of all words weighted by relevance — the V part of attention.
An edge means the two found each other interesting (mutual weight above epsilon); a triangle means three all found each other interesting, forming a tight group.
The 'party' analogy: each person looks (Q) at name-tags (K) and walks toward those whose tags match; the friend-groups that form are the simplices.
A triangle is where meaning gets 'composed' — three words pulled into one region form one combined concept.
methods_math: simplicial complex of 1- and 2-simplices via threshold epsilon
visualizations: Plotly 3D (3D scatter markers with labels, edge lines, and mesh3d triangles) with an eased animation interpolating words from their original to post-attention positions; sliders for sharpness and threshold epsilon; live sentence input; a simplex/edges/triangles info panel and a 'biggest move' readout.
internal_tensions: The 'attention' uses the identity as W (no learned projections), so it is a toy single-head model.
The claim that triangles = 'composed meaning' is a heuristic interpretation, not a demonstrated representational fact.

title: Der Leib — Hermann Schmitz interaktiv
category_reason: Interactive guide to Hermann Schmitz's philosophy/anthropology of the lived body; no ML.
thesis: In Hermann Schmitz's anthropology the 'Leib' (lived body) lives between tension (Engung) and expansion (Weitung), is not a continuous whole but a flux of blurred 'islands', and mediates these poles through irreversible bodily directions.
key_claims: The vital drive is tension against swelling (Schwellung) — the body oscillates between Engung (contraction) and Weitung (expansion).
The body is not a continuous whole but a 'Gewoge' (swell) of blurred islands without definite surfaces or borders (Leibesinseln).
Leibliche Richtung (bodily direction — e.g. gaze, exhale) is an irreversible direction from Enge toward Weite that mediates between the two.
Einleibung: two bodies connect through a common vital drive (antagonistic embodiment / bodily communication).
Perception splits into the protopathic (dull, blurred, dark) and the epikritic (pointed, sharp, light) poles.
visualizations: Five interactive canvases navigated by a bottom bar: Engung/Weitung (hold to contract), Leibesinseln (tap to spawn fading islands over a body outline), Leibliche Richtung (drag rays from center), Einleibung (drag two bodies together to connect), and a Protopathisch-<->-Epikritisch slider morphing soft blobs into sharp points.
internal_tensions: The body as a borderless field of islands opposes the body-as-bounded-object picture in physiology and cognition science.
Antagonistic embodiment (bodies binding through a shared drive) is a speculative anthropological claim.

title: Positional Encoding = Wave Interference (Wave Collapse)
category_reason: Visualizes transformer sinusoidal positional encoding as constructive wave interference.
thesis: Positional encoding can be read as wave interference: each frequency dimension is a source point on its circle that emits ripples, and where all ripples constructively overlap is the unique fingerprint of that position.
key_claims: Five frequency circles; the leftmost is the highest frequency (spins fast, encodes fine position differences) and the rightmost the lowest (spins slow, encodes coarse structure).
At each position the combination of angles across all circles is unique — like clock hands: the second hand distinguishes nearby positions, the hour hand distinguishes distant ones.
Each source emits cosine ripples that decay with distance; the field is the sum of all ripples, with bright zones = constructive (waves in phase) and dark zones = destructive.
This is analogous to how the dot product between two positional encodings captures their relative distance — nearby positions share similar bright zones.
methods_math: cosine ripple field with distance decay
visualizations: Canvas 2D pixel-level interference field plus the five circles, source points with ripple rings, a local-search 'wave collapse' convergence crosshair, a colored sin/cos encoding-vector readout, a token-position slider, and arrow-key / spacebar control for stepping and auto-play.
internal_tensions: The 'fingerprint'/'collapse' reading is an interpretive overlay; a position's identity is really the full vector of sin/cos values, not a single bright spot.
The interference-field rendering is computed per pixel each frame, so it is a heavy visualization.

title: Attention Heads als 'Augen'
category_reason: Explains transformer attention heads and the causal attention matrix with an interactive demo.
thesis: Each attention head is an 'eye' attending to a different aspect of token relations; the attention matrix (rows = query tokens 'I look from here', columns = key tokens 'I look there') can be read directly, with the causal mask zeroing the upper-right triangle.
key_claims: Rows of the matrix are Query tokens ('I look from here'), columns are Key tokens ('I look there'); each cell is that head's attention score for the pair.
The upper-right triangle is set to 0 by the causal mask — a token can only attend to itself and earlier tokens.

Eight hand-defined head 'scorers' model different behaviors: previous token, sentence start (BOS-like), self-reference, word-length match, repetition detector, far-back exponential decay, vowel-pattern similarity, and token-2-back.
Softmax is applied per row after masking, producing weights that sum to 1.
After attention each token gets a new vector that is the (causally limited) weighted sum of the context.
visualizations: An interactive HTML attention matrix with color-coded cells (click any cell for details), a legend of head-buttons (each with an emoji and behavior), a selectable head count, and an output-vector panel showing each token's weighted context aggregation; live sentence input.
internal_tensions: The heads are hand-coded toy scorers standing in for learned projections, so the 'specialization' is illustrative rather than empirical.
The 'eyes' metaphor risks over-reading intentionality into a linear-algebraic operation.

title: Attention Creates Simplicial Complexes
category_reason: Builds a simplicial complex (with Betti numbers) directly from transformer attention scores.
thesis: Type a sentence and each word gets a 3D embedding; attention scores (dot product) decide which words connect (edges) and which form triangles (2-simplices) — a simplicial complex that even yields Betti numbers, showing how meaning focuses locally.
key_claims: Each word maps to a 3D embedding [gender, being, power] in [-1,1] x [-1,1] x [0,1].
Attention is the dot product (a bilinear form with the identity), softmaxed row-wise with a sharpness (inverse temperature).
An edge is a pair whose mutual attention exceeds threshold epsilon; a triangle is three tokens all mutually connected.
Betti numbers are computed: beta_0 (connected components, via union-find) and beta_1 (loops) approximated as edges - (n - beta_0) - triangles.
Triangles mark where attention jointly composes three tokens into a single semantic focus — words 'thought about together'.
visualizations: Plotly 3D (3D scatter markers with labels, edge lines, mesh3d triangles), a token-embedding table, a simplicial-complex panel listing vertices/edges/triangles and Betti numbers with a meaning interpretation, and sliders for threshold epsilon and sharpness with live sentence input.
internal_tensions: The beta_1 formula is a rough approximation (edges - cyclomatic - triangles), not a proper homology computation.
A single simplified head (identity weights) is used, so the topological 'meaning' is heuristic.

title: Attention — Watch It Work
category_reason: Interactive visualization of the Q/K/V attention computation and information flow.
thesis: An interactive single-token attention flow: watch how a chosen query token aligns most with one key (smallest angle, highest weight) so its output is pulled toward that key's V vector; twisting the W_Q/W_K/W_V 'rotations' changes what counts as relevant versus what gets read.
key_claims: alpha_j = softmax(q . k_j / sqrt(d_k)) and output o = sum_j alpha_j v_j.
Q, K, and V are rotations of the same 2D token embeddings, controlled by W_Q / W_K / W_V twist sliders.
The query aligns most with the key whose angle to Q is smallest, giving it the largest weight and pulling the output toward that key's V vector.
Twisting W_Q / W_K changes what counts as relevant (the matching); twisting W_V changes what gets read (the content).
The 'focus' slider acts as softmax temperature, sharpening or flattening the weights.
visualizations: A canvas 2D three-zone scene: a left 'MATCHING (Q-K)' zone with angle arcs between the query and each key, a right 'READING (V)' zone with weight-sized circles and the output vector, and a middle of bezier 'pipes' whose thickness equals each weight; controls for which token asks, W_Q/W_K/W_V twist, and focus; a Temml math panel and a plain-English story line.
internal_tensions: The projection matrices are restricted to 2D rotations of hand-picked embeddings rather than learned, full-rank matrices.
A single query and single head are shown, so it illustrates the mechanics but not multi-head composition.

title: Layer als Raumkrümmung (A Layer Curves Space)
category_reason: Explains a neural layer as a nonlinear warp that makes non-separable data separable.
thesis: A neural network layer is a bending of space: a 2D dataset that is not linearly separable (inner core vs outer ring) becomes linearly separable once a layer lifts it into R^3 as phi(x,y) = (x, y, x^2 + y^2) and a plane slides between the classes — after which the plane collapses to a line and the space 'falls to a number'.
key_claims: Two classes (an inner point cloud and an outer ring) are not linearly separable in R^2 — no single straight cut separates them; topology forbids it.
Add a dimension: the old picture becomes the floor and a new z-axis stands up (embedding R^2 into R^3, no curvature yet).
The layer curves the space: phi(x,y) = (x, y, x^2 + y^2) — it bends, not tears; inner points sink, outer points rise into a shell.
A flat plane then slides cleanly between the classes in R^3, a linear separation w^T phi(x) + b = 0 that was impossible in 2D.
The plane is then squashed along the viewing direction into a line, and the space 'falls to a number' R^3 -> R, where a single point separates the classes.
methods_math: feature map / embedding into higher dimension
visualizations: A full-screen custom-projection canvas running a 7-step animated walkthrough (top view to side view camera moves, grid warping, the separating plane appearing and collapsing to a line, then a 1D score axis); navigate with arrow keys, drag to rotate, R to reset.
internal_tensions: It presents the canonical 'deep nets learn to warp space' story with a specific quadratic example, which is suggestive but not general (most real feature maps are far richer).
The 'plane becomes a line becomes a number' collapse is a visualization device that can overstate how a single scalar score is produced.
